Kim — quick pass from me.

Nice structure. A couple of quick items:
- Hero line: "Predictable LLM inference for product teams" reads a bit generic. Suggest stronger differentiation: "High-throughput LLM inference with enterprise SLAs" or "Low-latency, cost-controlled LLM inference for production apps".
- Second paragraph: move cost example into a small callout ("Typical: 5–8ms/ token on A100 with batching") only if we can validate those numbers with infra. Otherwise say "low-per-token economics".
- CTA: for marketplace, my vote is "Start a trial" if the offering supports a self-serve AMI trial. If it's gated, use "Request trial". Confirm with Ops/AMIs.

Also flagged two doc comments around legal phrasing — nothing major.

Ben

Hi Kim and team — thanks for the forward. Quick answers: 

1) CTA language: For AMI offers that require seller-side provisioning, we recommend "Request trial" or "Contact seller for trial". Use of "Start free trial" is reserved for self-serve/automated trials.

2) SLA & claims: You can reference SLA-backed targets if those are covered in your contract and clearly linked from the listing. Avoid precise per-token latency numbers unless you include a standard caveat ("typical results; actual performance varies based on workload and region").

Small copy notes:
- Avoid productized naming that references other vendors or generic model names ("GPT-4-style"). Use neutral model descriptors ("open and Redwood-verified model variants").
- Hero alt text: include short alt for accessibility for hero_asset_1200x400.png.

Attached our Marketplace listing checklist and seller copy guidelines (see attachment: aws_listing_checklist.pdf).

Let us know if you'd like us to review the final console copy before you submit.

Best,
Anjali Shah
AWS Marketplace Content Operations
aws-marketplace-content@amazon.com
